finding.sequence_description: JWT M2M: configure two OAuth Sources (one intended, one attacker-controlled) and test whether JWT login incorrectly accepts attacker-signed tokens due to overly-broad trust anchor selection (jwks_sources confusion).
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_other_source_jwt_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_other_source_jwt_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: JWT login accepted a token signed by a different (attacker-controlled) configured source; verification policy may be broader than the intended semantic trust anchor.

sequence.description: JWT M2M: configure two OAuth Sources (one intended, one attacker-controlled) and test whether JWT login incorrectly accepts attacker-signed tokens due to overly-broad trust anchor selection (jwks_sources confusion).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: JWT verification must be bound to the intended trust anchor(s). If only the intended source should be trusted, attacker-signed JWTs from a different configured source must be rejected; otherwise the broker is verifying a different proof policy than the one semantically intended.

finding.sequence_description: JWT trust-anchor rotation coherence: baseline JWT login succeeds with Source A JWKS; then update the OAuth Source JWKS URL (simulating key rotation) and re-save; old-key JWT should be rejected after the update.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: old_key_login_http_status >= 400
Evaluation: old_key_login_http_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After explicit JWKS update/re-save, authentik still accepted a JWT signed by the old key, indicating stale trust-anchor usage (config/runtime incoherence).

finding.sequence_description: Config-change coherence: obtain a token with broader scope, then tighten the application configuration and re-authenticate requesting the same scope; the tightened config should take effect immediately and reject/limit the flow.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_tighten_after_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_tighten_after_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After tightening application policy_engine_mode, re-authentication still succeeded as if old configuration was cached/stale (config-change flow coherence failure).

sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I3: Provider/application configuration changes must apply atomically to subsequent authentications; after tightening policy/engine mode, re-auth should not succeed under stale pre-change behavior.

finding.sequence_description: JWT M2M exp enforcement as authorization boundary: first a control JWT with exp in the future should succeed, then an expired JWT (exp in the past) should be rejected; acceptance would allow unauthorized continued access beyond intended lifetime.
finding.description: OIDC source login succeeded despite id_token issuer mismatch: the IdP returned an id_token with a different issuer than the source's configured OIDC well-known URL. This indicates the SP does not validate the iss claim per OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 Section 2.

sequence.description: JWT M2M exp enforcement as authorization boundary: first a control JWT with exp in the future should succeed, then an expired JWT (exp in the past) should be rejected; acceptance would allow unauthorized continued access beyond intended lifetime.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed upstream intent and broker policy; accepting an expired external JWT would extend authorization beyond its intended validity window (authorization binding to time constraints).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control case failed: valid exp JWT did not authenticate; setup/trust binding may be broken, making the expired-token result uninterpretable.
Expired external JWT was accepted, extending authorization beyond intended lifetime and violating authorization binding.
